PullRequest.Title: Revert "Browser: Remove duplicate border in Modern UI"

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or resizing an integrated browser editor in classic, Modern UI, or a floating window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: BrowserEditor.layoutBrowserContainer synchronously gathers contribution overrides, reads getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle, writes container geometry, then invokes model.layout; the service call reaches Electron main and WebContentsView.setBounds. The changed padding and pixel-snap arithmetic run on this path, but remain constant-time.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send browser bounds to Electron main and apply WebContentsView border radius/bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per editor layout invocation, plus at most two pre-existing frame retries only while dimensions are zero; no per-item collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff implementation made the same one layout service call per invocation after computing padding and snapping through extracted helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounds application is required to complete the visual layout, although the renderer does not await the returned promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with editor layout/resize/zoom event frequency and the number of browser editors being laid out, not page content size. The changed arithmetic is O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fire-and-forget layout service call per layoutBrowserContainer invocation; the pre-existing zero-size retry is bounded to two requestAnimationFrame retries. The diff does not add parallel calls, queues, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in bounds computation. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent; the diff neither adds cache misses nor defeats coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous DOM reads and single model.layout call are explicit in the traced call path, and the before/after diff shows no additional invocation on ordinary layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact resize-event frequency and IPC duration are not measured, but the diff removes DOM ancestor checks and does not increase boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The revert restores constant 3px padding and the prior floor-based snap calculation while removing two DOM closest checks; it does not add synchronous layout work or IPC calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing browser sharing state between user-only and agent-shared
Scenarios.CriticalPath: BrowserViewModel fires onDidChangeSharingState. Before the revert, the renderer listener synchronously called layoutBrowserContainer and issued a bounds update; the changed code removes that listener, so this feature contributes no work to the transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Deleted listener at src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/features/webContentsViewRendererFeature.ts:185 (LEFT) previously reached BrowserEditor.layoutBrowserContainer and model.layout
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute DOM geometry and send updated WebContentsView bounds to Electron main when sharing state changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one call per distinct sharing-state transition; after the diff, none from this renderer listener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff code registered onDidChangeSharingState and invoked a full browser-container relayout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The removed bounds update was on the sharing-state event path and could perform synchronous layout reads plus an IPC call; its removal reduces work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost previously scaled linearly with distinct sharing-state transitions; the diff reduces the multiplier to zero for this feature.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Previously one additional unawaited layout service call per distinct sharing-state transition; after the diff, zero from WebContentsViewRendererFeature. Sharing-state updates are discrete user/agent actions rather than a collection fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: BrowserViewModel suppresses unchanged sharing states before firing the event. No cache or negative-cache behavior is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both the deleted listener and the downstream layout/IPC path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sharing transitions are likely infrequent, so the size of the improvement is uncertain; there is nevertheless no regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. This change removes repeated synchronous layout and IPC work rather than introducing it; any visual consequence of no longer relayouting is correctness-only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enabling, resizing, or scaling device emulation in the integrated browser
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Emulation events call layoutBrowserContainer, the emulation contribution computes viewport dimensions, and the renderer contribution snaps the result before one model.layout call applies screen emulation and WebContentsView bounds in Electron main.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send emulated dimensions to main, apply Chromium screen emulation, and set native view bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary call per emulation-triggered relayout, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same emulation-triggered layout call and main-process operations occurred; pre-diff snapping used an extracted helper and retained 3px padding whenever device emulation was active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the emulated viewport to reflect the selected device or scale.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with user scale/device changes and pane resize frequency; layout arithmetic remains O(1), independent of page or history size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One unawaited layout call per scale/device/layout event. There is no added batching change, fan-out, or concurrency burst in the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. Device layout is recomputed on every relevant event both before and after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: emulation event call sites and the renderer-to-main path are directly traced, and the diff preserves the same boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured cost for Chromium applyScreenEmulation is available, but call count and event placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The restored computation changes rounding semantics only and does not add work, calls, retention, or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. The runtime changes restore constant padding and prior O(1) snapping, remove DOM ancestor checks, and remove a sharing-state-triggered relayout. All traced native-view layout boundaries are unchanged or reduced; the deleted test has no runtime impact. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.
